_comment: Reply box test vector (#4675, docs/design/reply-mailbox.md). A reply box is a club of two made by the sender's phone with each share link. K is the box's secret; it never leaves the phone. The four values come from HKDF-SHA-256 over K with an empty salt and the club info strings (sm-club-id-v1, -read-v1, -post-v1, -seal-v1), exactly as club-sealing-vector.json. The reply part is JSON {v,box,post,seal} sealed with the LINK key as SMLINK part 4 (additional data = the 8-byte header only, as for preview part 1 and packet part 2), served at GET /l/<id>/reply. An answer is a club post: SMLINK part 2 sealed with the seal key, additional data = header || 16 box id bytes. uploadHeaders are what the phone adds to POST /api/v1/links. Made once by a Go program from fixed bytes; Go, Swift and web tests check it. Not a real box: never reuse these keys.
